text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Farooq Leghari promulgated the Accountability Ordinance for corrupt officials and politicians to be tried by high courts.

- The caretaker government could set up a commission to investigate allegations that extrajudicial killings took place in Karachi, President Farooq Leghari told a news conference. He also endorsed the foreign policy of the deposed government of Benazir Bhutto.
- Furnace oil prices were raised 180 rupees to 6,296 rupees per tonne.
- Pakistan Muslim League chief Nawaz Sharif demanded army supervision of elections to prevent rigging.
- Pakistan railways decided to close two train services and suspend operation of 36 trains on Fridays and other holidays to reduce down its budget deficit.
- Deposed prime minister Benazir Bhutto has urged her arch-rival Nawaz Sharif to discuss with her how to save parliamentary democracy and the country from a big crisis.
- The caretaker government has decided to review all privatisation deals of the previous government and apprehend all those who were involved in shady transactions.
- President Farooq Leghari will announce a package of structural reforms in the second week of December after its approval by the International Monetary Fund.

- The government is working to expand the scope of privatisation in the transport sector including airlines, railways, shipping and airports, Chairman of the Privatisation Commission Salman Shah said.
- Nine U.S.-based companies have offered to finance projects worth $20 billion for infrastructure development, housing and transport, the state's Board of Investment said.
- The Commerce Ministry decided to review the gold import policy and give more licences for import of gold and silver.
- The Pakistan Credit Rating Agency Ltd has assigned A-3 rating to the First Grindlays Modaraba (Islamic mutual fund).
